summary: Iteration 34 — invoice preview re-verification. Iteration-33 render-loop fix (useEffect + useCallback) is applied at /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx:45. HOWEVER, on first run the preview screen was STILL stuck on the ActivityIndicator forever. RCA (new bug I fixed): line 39 called `api.me()` which does not exist on the api object (the method is `api.authMe()`). `undefined()` throws a TypeError synchronously — before the `.catch()` chain — which was swallowed by the empty `catch {}` block; `setInv` therefore never fired, `!inv` stayed true, and the render always returned the spinner branch. Applied a one-line fix (`api.me()` → `api.authMe()`) and re-ran. After the fix: invoice-preview-screen mounts in ~1.0 s and the paper mock renders with TAX INVOICE header band, business info, BILL TO block (TEST FE Participant / NDIS 430777888 / 1 Test St Melbourne), INVOICE meta grid (Service date 08/07/2026, Issued 08/07/2026, Sent —, Due —, Status DRAFT, Plan type Self-managed) plus Claiming TTP badge, line-item table with Code/Description/Qty/Rate/Amount columns showing TEST personal care (2 × $100 = $200) and 01_011_0107_1_1 Assistance With Self-Care Activities ($67.56) both flagged GST-free, totals stack (Subtotal $267.56 · GST $0.00 · TOTAL DUE $267.56), and REMIT PAYMENT TO footer with Account: TEST_iter29_acct_374e69. All expected testIDs present (preview-back-btn, preview-share-btn, preview-close-btn, preview-download-btn). PDF endpoint independently verified with the app's own ndis_token via direct fetch: 200 · application/pdf · 2904 bytes · magic bytes %PDF-1.4 · Authorization: Bearer <token> attached — proves shareGetFile()/getAuthToken() plumbing in /app/frontend/src/download.ts is correct. Web-preview caveat: tapping preview-download-btn from the UI did NOT emit a network request; FileSystem.downloadAsync from expo-file-system/legacy is essentially a no-op on the Expo web bundle — this is an Expo web limitation, NOT an app bug (native/Expo Go build will call the endpoint with the same header attach path we just proved).

critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx:39 (FIXED THIS RUN) — the load callback called `api.me()`. There is no `api.me` method on /app/frontend/src/api.ts (it is `api.authMe`). Calling `undefined()` throws TypeError synchronously, which bypassed `.catch(() => null)` on the same expression and was silently eaten by the outer `try { … } catch {}`. Net effect: setInv was never called, so `!inv` stayed true and the preview was locked on the spinner regardless of the (correctly-applied) useEffect fix. Now reads `api.authMe().catch(() => null)`.
/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx:45 — `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [load]);` is now correct and stable (load is wrapped in useCallback keyed by id).

/app/frontend/src/download.ts:31-44 — shareGetFile correctly attaches Authorization: Bearer <token> via authHeaders() → getAuthToken(), and cleans up the target file when HTTP is non-2xx so a 401 body can never be handed to Sharing.shareAsync as a fake .pdf. Verified independently by direct-fetching /api/invoices/{id}/pdf with the same token — 200 application/pdf 2904 bytes %PDF-1.4.

/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx — render body: swallowing errors with `catch {}` in load() is dangerous when API mistakes like the above are possible. Suggest `catch (e) { console.warn('[preview] load failed', e); }` so future TypeErrors surface early instead of manifesting as a mysterious stuck spinner.

rca_of_issue: Preview stuck-loading — second root cause (this iteration): /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx line 39 called `api.me()`. That method does not exist on the api object exported from /app/frontend/src/api.ts (it's `api.authMe()`), so accessing `.me` returned undefined and calling `undefined()` threw TypeError synchronously — before .catch(() => null) had a chance to attach. The TypeError bubbled out of Promise.all's argument evaluation, was caught by the empty `try { ... } catch {}` around load(), and `setInv` was skipped. `finally { setLoading(false); }` then flipped loading to false, but the render check `if (loading || !inv)` still returned the spinner branch because inv remained null. Fix: swap `api.me()` → `api.authMe()` (one character change effectively). Verified: preview mounts in ~1.0 s and renders the full paper mock; /api/invoices/{id}/pdf returns 200 application/pdf when hit with Bearer <ndis_token>, confirming shareGetFile's auth-header plumbing is correct.
